geometry.name: Subdivision
geometry.native_signature: type Subdivision is limited private;
geometry.source_signature:
--  An incremental Delaunay triangulation that exclusively owns one native
   --  cv::Subdiv2D. It is limited, so it cannot be copied; finalization
   --  releases the native object. A declared object is not ready until
   --  Create, Create_Float32, Reset or Reset_Float32 succeeds. A
   --  Subdivision must not be used by more than one task at a time, even
   --  for query-only operations; distinct objects are independent.
   type Subdivision is limited private;

geometry.name: Float32_Rectangle
Vertex_Id
geometry.native_signature: type Vertex_Id is range 0 .. 2**31 - 1;

geometry.name: Edge_Id
geometry.native_signature: type Edge_Id is range 0 .. 2**31 - 1;

geometry.name: Create
geometry.native_signature: function Create (Bounds : OpenCV.Rect) return Subdivision
geometry.source_signature:
--  A new Subdivision holding an empty Delaunay triangulation of Bounds,
   --  as if by Reset.
   --  @param Bounds Integer bounds, with the rules of Reset.
   --  @return A ready subdivision without inserted points.
   --  @exception OpenCV_Error Bounds that Reset rejects, or a native
   --    allocation or initialization failure.
   function Create (Bounds : OpenCV.Rect) return Subdivision;

geometry.name: Create_Float32
geometry.native_signature: function Create_Float32 (Bounds : Float32_Rectangle) return Subdivision
geometry.source_signature:
--  A new subdivision as if by Reset_Float32. The distinct name preserves
   --  integer Create calls with unqualified rectangle aggregates.
   --  @param Bounds Binary32 bounds, with the rules of Reset_Float32.
   --  @return A ready subdivision without inserted points.
   --  @exception OpenCV_Error Bounds that Reset_Float32 rejects, or a native
   --    allocation or initialization failure.
   function Create_Float32 (Bounds : Float32_Rectangle) return Subdivision;

geometry.name: Reset
geometry.native_signature: procedure Reset (Object : in out Subdivision; Bounds : OpenCV.Rect)
geometry.source_signature:
--  Discards every point and initializes Object to an empty Delaunay
   --  triangulation of Bounds, creating its native object when needed.
   --  Bounds.Width and Bounds.Height must be positive. OpenCV accepts points
   --  in the half-open region X >= Bounds.X, X < Bounds.X + Bounds.Width,
   --  and likewise for Y, with both limits computed in binary32 after native
   --  conversion of each integer field. Positive dimensions that disappear
   --  in this addition are rejected. Initialization arithmetic must produce
   --  finite upper limits and super-triangle coordinates. Semantic rejection
   --  leaves Object unchanged; native failure leaves it not ready. Neither
   --  failure publishes new bounds. Failures raise OpenCV.OpenCV_Error.
   --  Every vertex and edge identifier of Object becomes invalid.
   --  @param Object The subdivision to (re)initialize; it need not be ready.
   --  @param Bounds Integer bounds with positive Width and Height.
   --  @exception OpenCV_Error Bounds rejected by the rules above (Object
   --    unchanged), or a native allocation or initialization failure (Object
   --    not ready).
   procedure Reset (Object : in out Subdivision; Bounds : OpenCV.Rect);

geometry.name: Reset_Float32
geometry.native_signature:
procedure Reset_Float32
  (Object : in out Subdivision; Bounds : Float32_Rectangle)
geometry.source_signature:
--  As above, without rounding to integers. OpenCV 4.6 .. 4.12 uses a
   --  private initialization backport; 4.13+ and 5.x call native Rect2f.
   --  Is_Natively_Supported still reports native Rect2f availability only.
   --  All fields must be finite; Width and Height must be positive and their
   --  binary32 additions to X/Y must advance. `Big = 6 * max (Width,
   --  Height)` and X/Y +/- Big must remain finite. These conditions also
   --  guarantee a distinguishable, nondegenerate initial super-triangle, but
   --  not good conditioning of subsequent native geometric predicates.
   --  @param Object The subdivision to (re)initialize; it need not be ready.
   --  @param Bounds Binary32 bounds satisfying the rules above.
   --  @exception OpenCV_Error Bounds rejected by the rules above (Object
   --    unchanged), or a native allocation or initialization failure (Object
   --    not ready).
   procedure Reset_Float32
     (Object : in out Subdivision; Bounds : Float32_Rectangle);

geometry.name: Is_Ready
geometry.native_signature: function Is_Ready (Object : Subdivision) return Boolean
geometry.source_signature:
--  True when Object owns a native subdivision that accepts operations.
   --  False for an object that has never been Reset or Created, and after an
   --  operation that failed while modifying the triangulation, such as an
   --  insertion that exhausted memory, left it possibly inconsistent. Only
   --  Reset makes such an object ready again. Every other operation on a
   --  Subdivision except the bounds queries raises OpenCV.OpenCV_Error when
   --  the object is not ready.
   --  @param Object The subdivision to query.
   --  @return Whether Object can be used by the other operations.
   function Is_Ready (Object : Subdivision) return Boolean;

geometry.name: Bounds
geometry.native_signature: function Bounds (Object : Subdivision) return OpenCV.Rect
geometry.source_signature:
--  Original integer bounds of the last successful initialization. Raises
   --  OpenCV.OpenCV_Error when there has been none or Float32 bounds were
   --  supplied. Never silently rounds or encloses a Float32 rectangle.
   --  @param Object The subdivision to query; it need not be ready.
   --  @return The Bounds passed to the last successful Create or Reset.
   --  @exception OpenCV_Error No successful initialization yet, or the last
   --    one used Float32 bounds.
   function Bounds (Object : Subdivision) return OpenCV.Rect;

geometry.name: Bounds_Float32
geometry.native_signature: function Bounds_Float32 (Object : Subdivision) return Float32_Rectangle
geometry.source_signature:
--  Exact descriptor of the last successful initialization: the supplied
   --  Float32 rectangle, or each integer field converted as native OpenCV
   --  does. Upper limits are still computed by binary32 addition. Available
   --  on all releases, including after a failed native Reset; raises
   --  OpenCV.OpenCV_Error only when initialization has never succeeded.
   --  @param Object The subdivision to query; it need not be ready.
   --  @return The binary32 bounds of the last successful initialization.
   --  @exception OpenCV_Error No initialization has succeeded yet.
   function Bounds_Float32 (Object : Subdivision) return Float32_Rectangle;

geometry.name: Insert
geometry.native_signature:
function Insert
  (Object : in out Subdivision; Point : OpenCV.Float32_Point)
   return Vertex_Id
geometry.source_signature:
--  Inserts Point into the triangulation and returns its vertex. A point
   --  that OpenCV finds coincident with an existing vertex (binary32 L1
   --  distance below FLT_EPSILON from an endpoint of the edge where it is
   --  located) returns that vertex and adds nothing. Point must be finite
   --  and inside the bounds. A point outside the bounds, or a point that
   --  OpenCV cannot locate, raises OpenCV.OpenCV_Error and leaves the
   --  triangulation unchanged and Object ready. Every edge identifier of
   --  Object, and every Voronoi vertex, becomes invalid.
   --  @param Object A ready subdivision.
   --  @param Point The point to insert; finite and inside the bounds.
   --  @return The vertex of Point, or of the existing coincident vertex.
   --  @exception OpenCV_Error A non-finite Point, an Object that is not
   --    ready, a point outside the bounds or that OpenCV cannot locate, or
   --    another native failure (after which Object may be not ready).
   function Insert
     (Object : in out Subdivision; Point : OpenCV.Float32_Point)
      return Vertex_Id;

geometry.name: Insert
geometry.native_signature:
procedure Insert
  (Object : in out Subdivision; Points : Float32_Point_Array)
geometry.source_signature:
--  Inserts Points in iteration order, as repeated single insertions. Every
   --  coordinate is checked for finiteness before any point is inserted. When
   --  OpenCV rejects a point, for example because it lies outside the bounds,
   --  the points before it remain inserted and OpenCV.OpenCV_Error is raised.
   --  The insertion is therefore not atomic; the exception message names the
   --  index of the rejected point. Vertex identifiers are not returned: use
   --  the single-point Insert, Locate or Find_Nearest to obtain them.
   --  @param Object A ready subdivision.
   --  @param Points The points to insert, with any bounds; may be empty.
   --  @exception OpenCV_Error A non-finite coordinate (before any insertion),
   --    an Object that is not ready, or a rejected point, after which the
   --    earlier points remain inserted.
   procedure Insert
     (Object : in out Subdivision; Points : Float32_Point_Array);

geometry.name: Point_Location_Kind
geometry.native_signature: type Point_Location_Kind is (Inside_Facet, On_Edge, On_Vertex);
geometry.source_signature:
--  Classification of a located point.
   --  @enum Inside_Facet Strictly inside a facet (PTLOC_INSIDE).
   --  @enum On_Edge On an edge (PTLOC_ON_EDGE).
   --  @enum On_Vertex At an existing vertex (PTLOC_VERTEX).
   type Point_Location_Kind is (Inside_Facet, On_Edge, On_Vertex);

geometry.name: Locate_Result
geometry.source_signature:
--  Where a point lies in the triangulation:
   --  - Inside_Facet: inside the facet on the left of Edge. That facet can
   --    include reserved super-triangle vertices, as it does in a
   --    subdivision without points.
   --  - On_Edge: on Edge.
   --  - On_Vertex: at Vertex.
   --  @field Kind The classification, which selects the component.
   --  @field Edge For Inside_Facet, an edge with the facet on its left; for
   --    On_Edge, the edge containing the point.
   --  @field Vertex For On_Vertex, the vertex at the point.
   type Locate_Result (Kind : Point_Location_Kind := Inside_Facet) is record
      case Kind is
         when Inside_Facet | On_Edge =>
            Edge : Edge_Id;

         when On_Vertex =>
            Vertex : Vertex_Id;
      end case;
   end record;

geometry.name: Locate
geometry.native_signature:
function Locate
  (Object : in out Subdivision; Point : OpenCV.Float32_Point)
   return Locate_Result
geometry.source_signature:
--  Locates Point, which must be finite and inside the bounds. OpenCV
   --  raises an error for a point outside the bounds instead of returning its
   --  PTLOC_OUTSIDE_RECT classification, so such points raise
   --  OpenCV.OpenCV_Error, as does a search that does not converge. Locate
   --  updates OpenCV's cached search start, so the edge reported for a point
   --  can differ between calls.
   --  @param Object A ready subdivision; its cached search start changes.
   --  @param Point The point to locate; finite and inside the bounds.
   --  @return The classification with its edge, valid until the next Insert
   --    or Reset, or its vertex, valid until the next Reset.
   --  @exception OpenCV_Error A non-finite Point, an Object that is not
   --    ready, a point outside the bounds, a search that does not converge,
   --    or another native failure.
   function Locate
     (Object : in out Subdivision; Point : OpenCV.Float32_Point)
      return Locate_Result;

geometry.name: Nearest_Result
Find_Nearest
geometry.native_signature:
function Find_Nearest
  (Object : in out Subdivision; Point : OpenCV.Float32_Point)
   return Nearest_Result
geometry.source_signature:
--  The inserted vertex whose Voronoi facet contains Point, normally the
   --  nearest inserted vertex up to rounding, and its position. Numerical
   --  conditioning can affect this result (see Scale). Point must be finite
   --  and inside the bounds. Raises OpenCV.OpenCV_Error when no point has
   --  been inserted or when OpenCV reports no vertex; Object stays ready.
   --  Find_Nearest computes Voronoi data inside Object when earlier
   --  insertions invalidated it. It enters native OpenCV synchronously:
   --  cv::Subdiv2D::findNearest has an unbounded facet walk, and some
   --  numerically pathological triangulations can cause it not to return.
   --  The Ada binding cannot interrupt or recover from a native call that
   --  does not return. Reset can recover after a returned failure, but not
   --  while execution is stuck inside OpenCV. Callers requiring a hard
   --  liveness or deadline guarantee must not rely on Find_Nearest for
   --  untrusted or poorly conditioned geometry.
   --  @param Object A ready subdivision with at least one inserted point; its
   --    Voronoi data may be recomputed.
   --  @param Point The query point; finite and inside the bounds.
   --  @return The vertex whose Voronoi facet contains Point, with its
   --    position, when the native call returns. This is not proved to be the
   --    nearest inserted vertex.
   --  @exception OpenCV_Error A non-finite Point, an Object that is not
   --    ready, no inserted point, OpenCV reporting no vertex, or another
   --    native failure that returns; a call that does not return raises
   --    nothing.
   function Find_Nearest
     (Object : in out Subdivision; Point : OpenCV.Float32_Point)
      return Nearest_Result;

geometry.name: Edge_Segment
Edge_Segment_Array
geometry.native_signature: type Edge_Segment_Array is array (Natural range <>) of Edge_Segment;
geometry.source_signature:
--  Copied Delaunay edges, as returned by Edge_List.
   type Edge_Segment_Array is array (Natural range <>) of Edge_Segment;

geometry.name: Edge_Id_Array
geometry.native_signature: type Edge_Id_Array is array (Natural range <>) of Edge_Id;

geometry.name: Triangle_Array
geometry.native_signature:
type Triangle_Array is
  array (Natural range <>) of OpenCV.Geometry.Triangle_Vertices;

geometry.name: Edge_List
geometry.native_signature: function Edge_List (Object : Subdivision) return Edge_Segment_Array
geometry.source_signature:
--  Every Delaunay edge once, as by cv::Subdiv2D::getEdgeList. The list
   --  includes edges to the super-triangle vertices, whose positions lie
   --  outside the bounds, but not the super-triangle's own three edges.
   --  @param Object A ready subdivision.
   --  @return The edges in native order, indexed 1 .. N, as copied values
   --    that stay valid after later changes to Object.
   --  @exception OpenCV_Error An Object that is not ready, an invalid native
   --    count, or another native failure.
   function Edge_List (Object : Subdivision) return Edge_Segment_Array;

geometry.name: Leading_Edge_List
geometry.native_signature: function Leading_Edge_List (Object : Subdivision) return Edge_Id_Array
geometry.source_signature:
--  One edge of every triangular facet, as by getLeadingEdgeList, with the
   --  facet on its left, so three Next_Around_Left steps return to it. The
   --  facets include those with super-triangle vertices and the facet outside
   --  the super-triangle.
   --  @param Object A ready subdivision.
   --  @return The leading edges in native order, indexed 1 .. N. The array
   --    is Ada-owned, but its identifiers are valid only until the next
   --    Insert or Reset of Object.
   --  @exception OpenCV_Error An Object that is not ready, an invalid native
   --    count or edge, or another native failure.
   function Leading_Edge_List (Object : Subdivision) return Edge_Id_Array;

geometry.name: Triangle_List
geometry.native_signature: function Triangle_List (Object : Subdivision) return Triangle_Array
geometry.source_signature:
--  Every triangle whose three vertices all lie in the half-open bounds, as
   --  by getTriangleList, so triangles with a super-triangle vertex are
   --  excluded. Near the convex hull the reported triangles can differ
   --  between OpenCV releases: 4.12 and later, including 5.x, use a
   --  super-triangle twice as large as earlier releases.
   --  @param Object A ready subdivision.
   --  @return The triangles in native order, indexed 1 .. N, as copied
   --    vertex positions that stay valid after later changes to Object.
   --  @exception OpenCV_Error An Object that is not ready, an invalid native
   --    count, or another native failure.
   function Triangle_List (Object : Subdivision) return Triangle_Array;

geometry.name: Edge_Navigation
geometry.native_signature:
type Edge_Navigation is
  (Next_Around_Origin,
   Next_Around_Destination,
   Previous_Around_Origin,
   Previous_Around_Destination,
   Next_Around_Left,
   Next_Around_Right,
   Previous_Around_Left,
   Previous_Around_Right);
geometry.source_signature:
--  The eight related edges of cv::Subdiv2D::getEdge. For a Delaunay edge
   --  E the quad-edge structure gives these identities, which the binding's
   --  tests check on every supported release:
   --  - Next_Around_Origin (NEXT_AROUND_ORG, OpenCV's eOnext) and
   --    Previous_Around_Origin (PREV_AROUND_ORG) share E's origin;
   --  - Next_Around_Destination (NEXT_AROUND_DST, eDnext) and
   --    Previous_Around_Destination (PREV_AROUND_DST) share E's destination;
   --  - Next_Around_Left (NEXT_AROUND_LEFT, eLnext) and Previous_Around_Right
   --    (PREV_AROUND_RIGHT) start at E's destination;
   --  - Next_Around_Right (NEXT_AROUND_RIGHT, eRnext) and
   --    Previous_Around_Left (PREV_AROUND_LEFT) end at E's origin;
   --  - each Next choice and the matching Previous choice undo each other.
   --  @enum Next_Around_Origin NEXT_AROUND_ORG (eOnext): the next edge
   --    around E's origin, sharing that origin.
   --  @enum Next_Around_Destination NEXT_AROUND_DST (eDnext): the next edge
   --    around E's destination, sharing that destination.
   --  @enum Previous_Around_Origin PREV_AROUND_ORG: the previous edge around
   --    E's origin; it undoes Next_Around_Origin.
   --  @enum Previous_Around_Destination PREV_AROUND_DST: the previous edge
   --    around E's destination; it undoes Next_Around_Destination.
   --  @enum Next_Around_Left NEXT_AROUND_LEFT (eLnext): the next edge
   --    around E's left facet, starting at E's destination.
   --  @enum Next_Around_Right NEXT_AROUND_RIGHT (eRnext): the next edge
   --    around E's right facet, ending at E's origin.
   --  @enum Previous_Around_Left PREV_AROUND_LEFT: the previous edge around
   --    E's left facet, ending at E's origin; it undoes Next_Around_Left.
   --  @enum Previous_Around_Right PREV_AROUND_RIGHT: the previous edge
   --    around E's right facet, starting at E's destination; it undoes
   --    Next_Around_Right.
   type Edge_Navigation is
     (Next_Around_Origin,
      Next_Around_Destination,
      Previous_Around_Origin,
      Previous_Around_Destination,
      Next_Around_Left,
      Next_Around_Right,
      Previous_Around_Left,
      Previous_Around_Right);

geometry.name: Edge_Rotation
geometry.native_signature:
type Edge_Rotation is
  (Same_Edge, Rotated_Edge, Reversed_Edge, Reversed_Rotated_Edge);
geometry.source_signature:
--  The four edges of one quad-edge, as by cv::Subdiv2D::rotateEdge:
   --  Same_Edge is E itself, Rotated_Edge its dual (OpenCV's eRot), directed
   --  from the facet on E's right to the facet on its left, Reversed_Edge E
   --  with origin and destination swapped, and Reversed_Rotated_Edge the
   --  reversed dual. Four Rotated_Edge rotations return E.
   --  @enum Same_Edge The edge E itself.
   --  @enum Rotated_Edge The dual edge of E (OpenCV's eRot).
   --  @enum Reversed_Edge E with origin and destination swapped, as by
   --    symEdge.
   --  @enum Reversed_Rotated_Edge The reversed dual edge of E.
   type Edge_Rotation is
     (Same_Edge, Rotated_Edge, Reversed_Edge, Reversed_Rotated_Edge);

geometry.name: Navigate
geometry.native_signature:
function Navigate
  (Object : Subdivision; Edge : Edge_Id; Direction : Edge_Navigation)
   return Edge_Id
geometry.source_signature:
--  The edge related to Edge by Direction, as by getEdge.
   --  @param Object A ready subdivision.
   --  @param Edge An edge identifier produced by Object, at least 4.
   --  @param Direction The related edge to select.
   --  @return The related edge, valid until the next Insert or Reset.
   --  @exception OpenCV_Error An identifier of the reserved null edge, one
   --    beyond native storage, an Object that is not ready, OpenCV
   --    returning no edge, or another native failure.
   function Navigate
     (Object : Subdivision; Edge : Edge_Id; Direction : Edge_Navigation)
      return Edge_Id;

geometry.name: Next_Edge
geometry.native_signature: function Next_Edge (Object : Subdivision; Edge : Edge_Id) return Edge_Id
geometry.source_signature:
--  The next edge around Edge's origin, as by nextEdge; the same as
   --  Navigate (Object, Edge, Next_Around_Origin).
   --  @param Object A ready subdivision.
   --  @param Edge An edge identifier produced by Object, at least 4.
   --  @return The next edge around the origin, valid until the next Insert
   --    or Reset.
   --  @exception OpenCV_Error As for Navigate.
   function Next_Edge (Object : Subdivision; Edge : Edge_Id) return Edge_Id;

geometry.name: Rotate
geometry.native_signature:
function Rotate
  (Object : Subdivision; Edge : Edge_Id; Rotation : Edge_Rotation)
   return Edge_Id
geometry.source_signature:
--  The edge of Edge's quad-edge selected by Rotation, as by rotateEdge.
   --  @param Object A ready subdivision.
   --  @param Edge An edge identifier produced by Object, at least 4.
   --  @param Rotation Which of the four quad-edge members to return.
   --  @return The selected edge, valid until the next Insert or Reset.
   --  @exception OpenCV_Error As for Navigate.
   function Rotate
     (Object : Subdivision; Edge : Edge_Id; Rotation : Edge_Rotation)
      return Edge_Id;

geometry.name: Symmetric_Edge
geometry.native_signature:
function Symmetric_Edge
  (Object : Subdivision; Edge : Edge_Id) return Edge_Id
geometry.source_signature:
--  Edge with origin and destination swapped, as by symEdge; the same as
   --  Rotate (Object, Edge, Reversed_Edge).
   --  @param Object A ready subdivision.
   --  @param Edge An edge identifier produced by Object, at least 4.
   --  @return The reversed edge, valid until the next Insert or Reset.
   --  @exception OpenCV_Error As for Navigate.
   function Symmetric_Edge
     (Object : Subdivision; Edge : Edge_Id) return Edge_Id;

geometry.name: Origin
geometry.native_signature: function Origin (Object : Subdivision; Edge : Edge_Id) return Vertex_Id
geometry.source_signature:
--  The origin and destination vertices of Edge, as by edgeOrg and edgeDst.
   --  For a dual Voronoi edge they are the Voronoi vertices (circumcenters)
   --  of the facets it joins, which Find_Nearest and Voronoi_Facets compute
   --  and which are meaningful only until the next Insert. The result is
   --  No_Vertex before any Voronoi computation, and for a facet that OpenCV
   --  gives no Voronoi vertex: the facet outside the super-triangle, so one
   --  end of the dual of each super-triangle edge, and a degenerate facet
   --  whose circumcenter OpenCV cannot represent.
   --  @param Object A ready subdivision.
   --  @param Edge An edge identifier produced by Object, at least 4.
   --  @return The origin vertex of Edge, or No_Vertex as described above.
   --  @exception OpenCV_Error An identifier of the reserved null edge, one
   --    beyond native storage, an Object that is not ready, an invalid
   --    native vertex, or another native failure.
   function Origin (Object : Subdivision; Edge : Edge_Id) return Vertex_Id;

geometry.name: Destination
geometry.native_signature:
function Destination
  (Object : Subdivision; Edge : Edge_Id) return Vertex_Id
geometry.source_signature:
--  The destination vertex of Edge, as by edgeDst, with the same meaning
   --  for dual Voronoi edges and the same No_Vertex cases as Origin.
   --  @param Object A ready subdivision.
   --  @param Edge An edge identifier produced by Object, at least 4.
   --  @return The destination vertex of Edge, or No_Vertex as for Origin.
   --  @exception OpenCV_Error As for Origin.
   function Destination
     (Object : Subdivision; Edge : Edge_Id) return Vertex_Id;

geometry.name: Vertex_Point
geometry.native_signature:
function Vertex_Point
  (Object : Subdivision; Vertex : Vertex_Id) return OpenCV.Float32_Point
geometry.source_signature:
--  The position of Vertex, as by getVertex: an inserted point, one of the
   --  super-triangle vertices (identifiers 1 .. 3, outside the bounds), or a
   --  Voronoi vertex. Voronoi vertex positions are meaningful only until
   --  the next Insert.
   --  @param Object A ready subdivision.
   --  @param Vertex An occupied vertex slot of Object; not No_Vertex.
   --  @return The vertex position, as OpenCV stores it.
   --  @exception OpenCV_Error No_Vertex, a free slot, an identifier beyond
   --    native storage, an Object that is not ready, or another native
   --    failure.
   function Vertex_Point
     (Object : Subdivision; Vertex : Vertex_Id) return OpenCV.Float32_Point;

geometry.name: First_Edge
geometry.native_signature:
function First_Edge
  (Object : Subdivision; Vertex : Vertex_Id) return Edge_Id
geometry.source_signature:
--  An edge whose origin is Vertex, as recorded by OpenCV (getVertex's
   --  firstEdge), or No_Edge for a Voronoi vertex.
   --  @param Object A ready subdivision.
   --  @param Vertex An occupied vertex slot of Object; not No_Vertex.
   --  @return An edge leaving Vertex, valid until the next Insert or Reset,
   --    or No_Edge.
   --  @exception OpenCV_Error As for Vertex_Point, or an invalid native edge.
   function First_Edge
     (Object : Subdivision; Vertex : Vertex_Id) return Edge_Id;

geometry.name: Vertex_Id_Array
geometry.native_signature: type Vertex_Id_Array is array (Natural range <>) of Vertex_Id;
geometry.source_signature:
--  Vertex identifiers, such as the Sites of a Voronoi_Facets request.
   type Vertex_Id_Array is array (Natural range <>) of Vertex_Id;

geometry.name: Voronoi_Facet
geometry.source_signature:
--  One facet of a Voronoi_Diagram: Site, its position Site_Point (OpenCV's
   --  facet center), and the facet polygon, which is the diagram's
   --  Points (First .. Last) in the order of OpenCV's walk around Site.
   --
   --  Complete is False when OpenCV failed to create at least one Voronoi
   --  vertex for the facet, for example because degenerate or ill-conditioned
   --  geometry makes a circumcenter impossible to compute or represent in
   --  OpenCV's accepted finite binary32 range. Probes found missing vertices
   --  among points about 0.0001 to 0.003 units apart, depending on their
   --  distribution; these spacings are observations, not hard thresholds.
   --  OpenCV then reports the origin (0.0, 0.0) in place of each missing
   --  vertex, and the polygon keeps those placeholder points, so an
   --  incomplete polygon is not the true facet.
   --  @field Site The inserted point's vertex identifier.
   --  @field Site_Point The site's position, OpenCV's facet center.
   --  @field First Index in the diagram's Points of the polygon's first point.
   --  @field Last Index in the diagram's Points of the polygon's last point;
   --    at least First in a returned diagram.
   --  @field Complete False when the polygon holds placeholder points for
   --    Voronoi vertices that OpenCV failed to create.
   type Voronoi_Facet is record
      Site       : Vertex_Id := No_Vertex;
      Site_Point : OpenCV.Float32_Point := (X => 0.0, Y => 0.0);
      First      : Positive := 1;
      Last       : Natural := 0;
      Complete   : Boolean := True;
   end record;

geometry.name: Voronoi_Facet_Array
geometry.native_signature: type Voronoi_Facet_Array is array (Natural range <>) of Voronoi_Facet;
geometry.source_signature:
--  The facets of a Voronoi_Diagram, in diagram order.
   type Voronoi_Facet_Array is array (Natural range <>) of Voronoi_Facet;

geometry.name: Voronoi_Diagram
geometry.source_signature:
--  Facets indexed 1 .. Facet_Count and their points indexed
   --  1 .. Point_Count. The facet polygons are consecutive, nonempty slices
   --  of Points that follow facet order and together cover Points. The
   --  diagram is an Ada-owned copy; its Site identifiers follow the
   --  Vertex_Id lifetime rules, and positions near the super-triangle
   --  depend on the OpenCV release.
   --  @field Facet_Count Number of facets.
   --  @field Point_Count Total number of polygon points of all facets.
   --  @field Facets The facets, indexed 1 .. Facet_Count.
   --  @field Points All facet polygons, concatenated in facet order.
   type Voronoi_Diagram (Facet_Count, Point_Count : Natural) is record
      Facets : Voronoi_Facet_Array (1 .. Facet_Count);
      Points : Float32_Point_Array (1 .. Point_Count);
   end record;

geometry.name: Facet_Points
geometry.native_signature:
function Facet_Points
  (Diagram : Voronoi_Diagram; Index : Positive) return Float32_Point_Array
geometry.source_signature:
--  The polygon of Diagram.Facets (Index), indexed 1 .. N. Raises
   --  Constraint_Error when Index or that facet's slice lies outside Diagram.
   --  @param Diagram A Voronoi diagram, normally from Voronoi_Facets.
   --  @param Index A facet index in 1 .. Diagram.Facet_Count.
   --  @return A copy of that facet's polygon, indexed 1 .. N.
   --  @exception Constraint_Error Index outside Diagram.Facets, or a facet
   --    slice outside Diagram.Points (only in a diagram not built by
   --    Voronoi_Facets).
   function Facet_Points
     (Diagram : Voronoi_Diagram; Index : Positive) return Float32_Point_Array;

geometry.name: Voronoi_Facets
geometry.native_signature:
function Voronoi_Facets
  (Object : in out Subdivision) return Voronoi_Diagram
geometry.source_signature:
--  The facet of every inserted point, once each and in increasing Site
   --  order, as by cv::Subdiv2D::getVoronoiFacetList for every vertex. An
   --  object without inserted points gives an empty diagram.
   --  @param Object A ready subdivision; its Voronoi data may be recomputed.
   --  @return The diagram of every inserted point's facet.
   --  @exception OpenCV_Error An Object that is not ready, an inconsistent
   --    native result, or another native failure; Object stays ready after
   --    a native failure.
   function Voronoi_Facets
     (Object : in out Subdivision) return Voronoi_Diagram;

geometry.name: Voronoi_Facets

function Voronoi_Facets
  (Object : in out Subdivision; Sites : Vertex_Id_Array)

--  The facets of Sites, in order and once per occurrence, as by
   --  getVoronoiFacetList with Sites as its index list. Each element must be
   --  the vertex of an inserted point. No_Vertex, the super-triangle

   --  an empty index list as every vertex, empty Sites give an empty
   --  diagram.

   --  @return The facets of Sites in order, one per element.

   --    not ready, an inconsistent native result, or another native failure;
   --    Object stays ready after a native failure.
   function Voronoi_Facets
     (Object : in out Subdivision; Sites : Vertex_Id_Array)
      return Voronoi_Diagram;

geometry.name: Native_Feature
geometry.native_signature:
type Native_Feature is
  (Approximate_Convex_Polygon_Feature,
   Closest_Ellipse_Points_Feature,
   Minimum_Enclosing_Convex_Polygon_Feature,
   Float32_Subdivision_Bounds_Feature);
geometry.source_signature:
--  Availability in the linked native OpenCV, NOT Ada binding coverage.
   --  Approximate_Convex_Polygon and Minimum_Enclosing_Convex_Polygon remain
   --  unbound even when supported here. Every feature is available natively
   --  on OpenCV 5.x and from the 4.x release named below; earlier releases,
   --  including 4.6 and 4.10, report all four as unsupported.

   --    4.11; no Ada operation binds it.
   --  @enum Closest_Ellipse_Points_Feature Native
   --    cv::getClosestEllipsePoints, from 4.12. Closest_Ellipse_Points works
   --    on every supported release regardless.
   --  @enum Minimum_Enclosing_Convex_Polygon_Feature Native
   --    cv::minEnclosingConvexPolygon, from 4.13; no Ada operation binds it.
   --  @enum Float32_Subdivision_Bounds_Feature Native cv::Rect2f bounds for
   --    cv::Subdiv2D, from 4.13. OpenCV.Geometry.Subdiv2D accepts Float32
   --    bounds on every supported release regardless.

     (Approximate_Convex_Polygon_Feature,
      Closest_Ellipse_Points_Feature,
      Minimum_Enclosing_Convex_Polygon_Feature,
      Float32_Subdivision_Bounds_Feature);

geometry.name: Is_Natively_Supported

geometry.source_signature:
--  Whether the OpenCV release this binding was built against provides
   --  Feature natively. The answer is fixed by the native version at shim
   --  build time; it never reports whether an Ada operation exists, and a
   --  True result does not bind an unbound native function.

   --  @exception OpenCV_Error A failure reported by the shim query.
   function Is_Natively_Supported (Feature : Native_Feature) return Boolean;

geometry.name: Contour
geometry.native_signature: subtype Contour is OpenCV.Point_Array;
geometry.source_signature:
--  An integer contour or point set, for integer-coordinate geometry: an
   --  OpenCV.Point_Array passed to OpenCV as CV_32S points in index order.
   --  Inputs may have any bounds. Contour results are zero-based, or the
   --  null range 1 .. 0 when empty.
   subtype Contour is OpenCV.Point_Array;

geometry.name: Float32_Point_Array
geometry.native_signature:
type Float32_Point_Array is
  array (Natural range <>) of OpenCV.Float32_Point;
geometry.source_signature:
--  Ada-owned sequence of binary32 points: a point set for native subpixel
   --  geometry (OpenCV CV_32F, Point2f), an intersection region returned by
   --  OpenCV, or one side of a transform correspondence.
   --
   --  Operations overloaded for Float32_Point_Array call OpenCV's native
   --  CV_32F path, so coordinates are never rounded to integers. Every
   --  coordinate passed to them must be finite: NaN and infinities raise
   --  OpenCV_Error. Iteration order is native order, and bounds may be any
   --  Natural range. OpenCV computes coordinate differences, and for some
   --  operations their products, in binary32, so results can differ from
   --  those of integer-coordinate contours with the same shape; each overload
   --  states the native arithmetic that matters.
   type Float32_Point_Array is
     array (Natural range <>) of OpenCV.Float32_Point;

geometry.name: Closest_Ellipse_Points
geometry.native_signature:
function Closest_Ellipse_Points
  (Ellipse : OpenCV.Rotated_Rect; Points : Contour)
   return Float32_Point_Array
geometry.source_signature:
--  One approximate closest ellipse point per query, preserving
   --  Points'Range (including null and Natural'Last-adjacent ranges).
   --  Native on OpenCV 4.12+ and 5.x; a private compatibility implementation
   --  is used on 4.6--4.11. Empty input returns the same null range.
   --  Ellipse fields and Float32 queries must be finite; both ellipse
   --  dimensions must be positive. Native arithmetic has three fixed
   --  iterations: extreme inputs can produce non-finite output, rejected
   --  with OpenCV_Error. No arbitrary coordinate limit is imposed.
   --  Integer queries enter CV_32S and OpenCV converts them to Point2f,
   --  possibly losing low bits. Both overloads return Float32 points.
   --  Ellipse and Points are unchanged.
   --  @param Ellipse The ellipse as the rotated rectangle in which it is
   --    inscribed (full axis lengths, angle in degrees); every field finite,
   --    width and height positive.
   --  @param Points Query points, with any bounds, including a null range.
   --  @return For each query, at the same index, its approximate closest
   --    point on the ellipse: the result has exactly the bounds of Points
   --    (the postcondition), and every coordinate is finite.
   --  @exception OpenCV_Error A non-finite Ellipse field, a nonpositive
   --    width or height, more than Integer_32'Last points, a non-finite
   --    native point, or a failure reported by OpenCV.
   function Closest_Ellipse_Points
     (Ellipse : OpenCV.Rotated_Rect; Points : Contour)
      return Float32_Point_Array
   with
     Post =>
       Closest_Ellipse_Points'Result'First = Points'First
       and then Closest_Ellipse_Points'Result'Last = Points'Last;

geometry.name: Closest_Ellipse_Points
geometry.native_signature:
function Closest_Ellipse_Points
  (Ellipse : OpenCV.Rotated_Rect; Points : Float32_Point_Array)
   return Float32_Point_Array
geometry.source_signature:
--  Closest_Ellipse_Points for binary32 queries, which reach OpenCV as
   --  CV_32F without rounding, with the same native and compatibility
   --  implementations, Ellipse rules and empty-input result as the integer
   --  overload. Every query coordinate must be finite. Ellipse and Points
   --  are unchanged.
   --  @param Ellipse The ellipse as the rotated rectangle in which it is
   --    inscribed; every field finite, width and height positive.
   --  @param Points Query points, with any bounds; every coordinate finite.
   --  @return For each query, at the same index, its approximate closest
   --    point on the ellipse: the result has exactly the bounds of Points
   --    (the postcondition), and every coordinate is finite.
   --  @exception OpenCV_Error A non-finite Ellipse field or query
   --    coordinate, a nonpositive width or height, more than
   --    Integer_32'Last points, a non-finite native point, or a failure
   --    reported by OpenCV.
   function Closest_Ellipse_Points
     (Ellipse : OpenCV.Rotated_Rect; Points : Float32_Point_Array)
      return Float32_Point_Array
   with
     Post =>
       Closest_Ellipse_Points'Result'First = Points'First
       and then Closest_Ellipse_Points'Result'Last = Points'Last;

geometry.name: Contour_Area
geometry.native_signature:
function Contour_Area
  (Points : Contour; Oriented : Boolean := False)
   return OpenCV.Float64_Value
geometry.source_signature:
--  Calculates the OpenCV polygon area of Points with cv::contourArea.
   --  When Oriented is False, the result is nonnegative; otherwise it
   --  retains OpenCV's orientation sign. Empty and degenerate contours

   --    be empty.
   --  @param Oriented False for the absolute area; True for OpenCV's signed
   --    area, whose sign depends on the traversal direction.
   --  @return The area in binary64, as OpenCV computes it.
   --  @exception OpenCV_Error More than Integer_32'Last points, or a failure
   --    reported by OpenCV.
   function Contour_Area
     (Points : Contour; Oriented : Boolean := False)
      return OpenCV.Float64_Value;

geometry.name: Contour_Area
geometry.native_signature:
function Contour_Area
  (Points : Float32_Point_Array; Oriented : Boolean := False)
   return OpenCV.Float64_Value
geometry.source_signature:
--  Contour_Area of a Float32 point set. OpenCV accumulates the cross
   --  products of the binary32 coordinates in binary64, so the result is
   --  always finite. Points is unchanged.
   --  @param Points Polygon vertices in traversal order, with any bounds;
   --    every coordinate must be finite. May be empty.
   --  @param Oriented False for the absolute area; True for OpenCV's signed
   --    area, whose sign depends on the traversal direction.
   --  @return The area in binary64, as OpenCV computes it.
   --  @exception OpenCV_Error A NaN or infinite coordinate, more than
   --    Integer_32'Last points, or a failure reported by OpenCV.
   function Contour_Area
     (Points : Float32_Point_Array; Oriented : Boolean := False)
      return OpenCV.Float64_Value;

geometry.name: Arc_Length
geometry.native_signature:
function Arc_Length
  (Points : Contour; Closed : Boolean) return OpenCV.Float64_Value
geometry.source_signature:
--  Calculates the OpenCV curve length of Points with cv::arcLength.
   --  Closed includes the segment from the final point to the first. Empty
   --  and one-point contours return zero. Points is unchanged.
   --  @param Points Curve vertices in order, with any bounds; may be empty.
   --  @param Closed True to include the closing segment from the last point
   --    back to the first.
   --  @return The nonnegative length in binary64, as OpenCV computes it.
   --  @exception OpenCV_Error More than Integer_32'Last points, or a failure
   --    reported by OpenCV.
   function Arc_Length
     (Points : Contour; Closed : Boolean) return OpenCV.Float64_Value;

geometry.name: Arc_Length
geometry.native_signature:
function Arc_Length
  (Points : Float32_Point_Array; Closed : Boolean)
   return OpenCV.Float64_Value
geometry.source_signature:
--  Arc_Length of a Float32 point set. OpenCV computes each segment's
   --  coordinate differences, their squares, and the segment length in
   --  binary32 and sums the lengths in binary64. A segment longer than about
   --  1.8E+19 overflows binary32 and makes the native length infinite, which
   --  raises OpenCV_Error; segment components below about 1.0E-19 lose
   --  precision as their squares underflow. Points is unchanged.
   --  @param Points Curve vertices in order, with any bounds; every
   --    coordinate must be finite. May be empty.
   --  @param Closed True to include the closing segment from the last point
   --    back to the first.
   --  @return The nonnegative, finite length in binary64.
   --  @exception OpenCV_Error A NaN or infinite coordinate, more than
   --    Integer_32'Last points, an infinite native length, or a failure
   --    reported by OpenCV.
   function Arc_Length
     (Points : Float32_Point_Array; Closed : Boolean)
      return OpenCV.Float64_Value;

geometry.name: Moments_Result
Compute_Moments
geometry.native_signature: function Compute_Moments (Points : Contour) return Moments_Result
geometry.source_signature:
--  Spatial, central, and normalized central moments through third order
   --  of the polygon Points, computed by cv::moments. For ordinary
   --  non-self-intersecting contours, M_00 is the polygon area. A centroid,
   --  when meaningful, is (M_10 / M_00, M_01 / M_00); callers must handle
   --  M_00 = 0.0 themselves. Self-intersecting contours may have surprising
   --  moments because OpenCV uses Green's formula. Empty contours return an
   --  all-zero result. Points is unchanged.
   --  @param Points Polygon vertices in traversal order, with any bounds; may
   --    be empty.
   --  @return The native moments of the polygon.
   --  @exception OpenCV_Error More than Integer_32'Last points, or a failure
   --    reported by OpenCV.
   function Compute_Moments (Points : Contour) return Moments_Result;

geometry.name: Compute_Moments
geometry.native_signature:
function Compute_Moments
  (Points : Float32_Point_Array) return Moments_Result
geometry.source_signature:
--  Compute_Moments of a Float32 point set. OpenCV evaluates Green's
   --  formula in binary64 from the binary32 coordinates. When the magnitude
   --  of OpenCV's computed doubled area is at most FLT_EPSILON
   --  (`2.0**(-23)`), that is, for an absolute area of at most about 6.0E-8,
   --  every field is 0.0; an integer contour never has such a nonzero area,
   --  but a small Float32 one can. Non-finite native moments, which extreme
   --  coordinates can produce, for example in a self-intersecting contour
   --  whose net area is tiny, raise OpenCV_Error. Points is unchanged.
   --  @param Points Polygon vertices in traversal order, with any bounds;
   --    every coordinate must be finite. May be empty.
   --  @return The native moments, every field finite.
   --  @exception OpenCV_Error A NaN or infinite coordinate, more than
   --    Integer_32'Last points, a non-finite native moment, or a failure
   --    reported by OpenCV.
   function Compute_Moments
     (Points : Float32_Point_Array) return Moments_Result;

geometry.name: Hu_Moment_Index
geometry.native_signature: type Hu_Moment_Index is range 1 .. 7;
geometry.source_signature:
--  Position of a Hu invariant: index I holds OpenCV's hu[I - 1].
   type Hu_Moment_Index is range 1 .. 7;

geometry.name: Hu_Moments_Result
geometry.native_signature: type Hu_Moments_Result is array (Hu_Moment_Index) of OpenCV.Float64_Value;
geometry.source_signature:
--  The seven Hu invariants, indexed in OpenCV order.
   type Hu_Moments_Result is array (Hu_Moment_Index) of OpenCV.Float64_Value;

geometry.name: Hu_Moments
geometry.native_signature: function Hu_Moments (Moments : Moments_Result) return Hu_Moments_Result
geometry.source_signature:
--  Seven Hu invariants of Moments in OpenCV order, indexed 1 .. 7, by
   --  cv::HuMoments. The values are the raw invariants, not logarithmically
   --  transformed Match_Shapes scores. They are invariant to translation,
   --  scale, rotation, and reflection except the seventh, whose sign changes
   --  under reflection. Rasterized-image transforms can differ slightly.
   --  Compose with Compute_Moments as Hu_Moments (Compute_Moments (Points)).
   --  Moments is unchanged.
   --  @param Moments Moments, normally from Compute_Moments; OpenCV uses its
   --    normalized central moments. Every field must be finite: a
   --    non-finite field, which only invalid data can hold, raises
   --    OpenCV_Error.
   --  @return The seven finite invariants.
   --  @exception OpenCV_Error A non-finite field of Moments, a native Hu
   --    value that is not finite and so cannot be represented by
   --    Float64_Value, or a failure reported by OpenCV.
   function Hu_Moments (Moments : Moments_Result) return Hu_Moments_Result;

geometry.name: Hull_Orientation
geometry.native_signature: type Hull_Orientation is (Counterclockwise, Clockwise);
geometry.source_signature:
--  Orientation of a convex hull result, in OpenCV's convention: X
   --  increases rightward and Y increases upward. Image coordinates often
   --  increase Y downward, so the visual winding may appear reversed.
   --  @enum Counterclockwise Counterclockwise order, OpenCV's default
   --    (clockwise = false).
   --  @enum Clockwise Clockwise order (OpenCV clockwise = true).
   type Hull_Orientation is (Counterclockwise, Clockwise);

geometry.name: Convex_Hull
geometry.native_signature:
function Convex_Hull
  (Points : Contour; Orientation : Hull_Orientation := Counterclockwise)
   return Contour
geometry.source_signature:
--  Convex hull of Points as an Ada-owned contour of hull points, not
   --  source-point indices, computed by cv::convexHull. Empty input returns
   --  an empty contour. Points is unchanged. More than Integer_32'Last - 2
   --  points raise OpenCV_Error because native convexHull computes total + 2
   --  in signed int before stack allocation, and so do inputs whose native
   --  signed 32-bit hull arithmetic would overflow.
   --  @param Points The point set, with any bounds; may be empty.
   --  @param Orientation Winding of the result, counterclockwise by default.
   --  @return The hull vertices, copied from Points, in the requested
   --    winding: zero-based, or the null range 1 .. 0 for empty input.
   --  @exception OpenCV_Error Too many points, coordinates that would
   --    overflow native hull arithmetic, or a failure reported by OpenCV.
   function Convex_Hull
     (Points : Contour; Orientation : Hull_Orientation := Counterclockwise)
      return Contour;

geometry.name: Convex_Hull
geometry.native_signature:
function Convex_Hull
  (Points      : Float32_Point_Array;
   Orientation : Hull_Orientation := Counterclockwise)
   return Float32_Point_Array
geometry.source_signature:
--  Convex hull of a Float32 point set as an Ada-owned Float32 point set,
   --  zero-based like the integer result; empty input returns the null
   --  range 1 .. 0. Hull points are copies of input points, never rounded,
   --  except that OpenCV receives each -0.0 coordinate as +0.0: native
   --  convexHull compares its extreme points bitwise, so a set of equal
   --  points mixing +0.0 and -0.0 would otherwise yield an empty hull. The
   --  orientation convention is the integer overload's. OpenCV compares
   --  binary32 coordinate differences through binary64 cross products, and
   --  OpenCV 5.x first normalizes those differences to unit vectors, so
   --  nearly collinear points can be kept or dropped differently by OpenCV
   --  4.x and 5.x. So that no difference overflows, the X span and the Y
   --  span of Points, computed in binary64, must each be at most
   --  Float32_Value'Last; wider sets raise OpenCV_Error. Points is
   --  unchanged. More than Integer_32'Last - 2 points raise OpenCV_Error
   --  because native convexHull computes total + 2 in signed int.
   --  @param Points The point set, with any bounds; every coordinate must be
   --    finite. May be empty.
   --  @param Orientation Winding of the result, counterclockwise by default.
   --  @return The hull vertices in the requested winding.
   --  @exception OpenCV_Error A NaN or infinite coordinate, too many points,
   --    an X or Y span above Float32_Value'Last, a non-finite native vertex,
   --    or a failure reported by OpenCV.
   function Convex_Hull
     (Points      : Float32_Point_Array;
      Orientation : Hull_Orientation := Counterclockwise)
      return Float32_Point_Array;

geometry.name: Point_Index_Array
geometry.native_signature: type Point_Index_Array is array (Natural range <>) of Natural;

geometry.name: Convex_Hull_Indices
geometry.native_signature:
function Convex_Hull_Indices
  (Points : Contour; Orientation : Hull_Orientation := Counterclockwise)
   return Point_Index_Array
geometry.source_signature:
--  Convex hull of Points as indices into Points. Every value is an index
   --  in Points'Range, not a native zero-based offset, so shifted and other
   --  nonzero Points bounds are preserved. The indices describe the same
   --  hull as Convex_Hull with the same Orientation. OpenCV cyclically
   --  shifts the sequence to be strictly increasing or strictly decreasing
   --  when possible, which holds for simple contours; a self-intersecting
   --  contour may yield a sequence that is neither. When several points
   --  share one hull vertex's coordinates, any of their indices may be
   --  returned, and OpenCV 4.x and 5.x can choose differently. Points is
   --  unchanged. Inputs that would overflow native integer convex-hull
   --  arithmetic raise OpenCV_Error, including more than Integer_32'Last - 2
   --  points because native convexHull computes total + 2 in signed int.
   --  @param Points The point set, with any bounds; may be empty.
   --  @param Orientation Winding of the hull, counterclockwise by default.
   --  @return The hull as indices in Points'Range, at most Points'Length of
   --    them (the postcondition): zero-based, or the null range 1 .. 0 for
   --    empty input.
   --  @exception OpenCV_Error Too many points, coordinates that would
   --    overflow native hull arithmetic, a native index outside Points, or a
   --    failure reported by OpenCV.
   function Convex_Hull_Indices
     (Points : Contour; Orientation : Hull_Orientation := Counterclockwise)
      return Point_Index_Array
   with
     Post =>
       Convex_Hull_Indices'Result'Length <= Points'Length
       and then (for all Index of Convex_Hull_Indices'Result =>
                   Index in Points'Range);

geometry.name: Convex_Hull_Indices
geometry.native_signature:
function Convex_Hull_Indices
  (Points      : Float32_Point_Array;
   Orientation : Hull_Orientation := Counterclockwise)
   return Point_Index_Array
geometry.source_signature:
--  Convex hull of a Float32 point set as indices in Points'Range,
   --  describing the same hull as the Float32 Convex_Hull with the same
   --  Orientation, under the same count limit (Integer_32'Last - 2 points,
   --  due to native signed total + 2), rules for signed zeros and spans,
   --  and OpenCV 4.x and 5.x differences. Among points with equal coordinates,
   --  any index may be returned. Points is unchanged.
   --  @param Points The point set, with any bounds; every coordinate must be
   --    finite. May be empty.
   --  @param Orientation Winding of the hull, counterclockwise by default.
   --  @return The hull as indices in Points'Range, at most Points'Length of
   --    them (the postcondition): zero-based, or the null range 1 .. 0 for
   --    empty input.
   --  @exception OpenCV_Error A NaN or infinite coordinate, too many points,
   --    an X or Y span above Float32_Value'Last, a native index outside
   --    Points, or a failure reported by OpenCV.
   function Convex_Hull_Indices
     (Points      : Float32_Point_Array;
      Orientation : Hull_Orientation := Counterclockwise)
      return Point_Index_Array
   with
     Post =>
       Convex_Hull_Indices'Result'Length <= Points'Length
       and then (for all Index of Convex_Hull_Indices'Result =>
                   Index in Points'Range);

geometry.name: Convexity_Defect
geometry.source_signature:
--  A region where Points departs inward from one hull edge. Start_Index
   --  and End_Index are the hull vertices bounding that edge, and
   --  Farthest_Index is the contour point between them farthest from the
   --  edge's line; all three are indices in Points'Range. Depth is that
   --  distance at OpenCV's 1/256 fixed-point resolution: the native
   --  fixed-point value divided by 256.0, which is exactly representable.
   --  Depth is nonnegative; a defect shallower than 1/512 reports 0.0.
   --  @field Start_Index Index in Points'Range of the hull vertex where the
   --    defect begins.
   --  @field End_Index Index in Points'Range of the hull vertex where the
   --    defect ends.
   --  @field Farthest_Index Index in Points'Range of the contour point
   --    farthest from the hull edge.
   --  @field Depth Distance of that point from the edge's line, a multiple
   --    of 1/256.
   type Convexity_Defect is record
      Start_Index    : Natural := 0;
      End_Index      : Natural := 0;
      Farthest_Index : Natural := 0;
      Depth          : OpenCV.Float64_Value := 0.0;
   end record;

geometry.name: Convexity_Defect_Array
geometry.native_signature: type Convexity_Defect_Array is array (Natural range <>) of Convexity_Defect;
geometry.source_signature:
--  Convexity defects in the order OpenCV reports them.
   type Convexity_Defect_Array is array (Natural range <>) of Convexity_Defect;

geometry.name: Convexity_Defects
geometry.native_signature:
function Convexity_Defects
  (Points : Contour; Hull : Point_Index_Array) return Convexity_Defect_Array
geometry.source_signature:
--  Convexity defects of Points relative to Hull, a sequence of indices in
   --  Points'Range such as the result of Convex_Hull_Indices. Hull must be
   --  strictly increasing or strictly decreasing; out-of-range, repeated,
   --  or otherwise non-monotonic indices raise OpenCV_Error. Hull is not
   --  checked to be the convex hull of Points: defects are measured against
   --  the edges between consecutive Hull indices, including the closing
   --  edge. Both Hull directions give the same result, ordered by OpenCV:
   --  the closing edge from the largest to the smallest Hull index first,
   --  then edges in ascending index order. Points should be a simple
   --  contour. After Hull is validated, a Points of at most three points or
   --  a Hull of fewer than three indices yields an empty result. Otherwise
   --  the X and Y spans of Points, Width and Height, must satisfy
   --  `Width**2 + Height**2 <= 8_388_607**2`, where 8_388_607 is
   --  Integer_32'Last / 256: OpenCV stores Depth * 256 rounded in a signed
   --  32-bit integer, and no Depth exceeds the bounding-box diagonal. This
   --  also keeps native signed 32-bit coordinate subtraction from
   --  overflowing. Larger spans raise OpenCV_Error before native code runs.
   --  Points and Hull are unchanged.
   --  @param Points A simple contour, with any bounds.
   --  @param Hull Strictly monotonic indices in Points'Range, normally
   --    Convex_Hull_Indices (Points).
   --  @return The defects, ordered by OpenCV, with every index in
   --    Points'Range and at most Hull'Length defects (the postcondition):
   --    zero-based, or the null range 1 .. 0 when there are none.
   --  @exception OpenCV_Error A Hull index outside Points'Range, a repeated
   --    or non-monotonic Hull, spans beyond the fixed-point depth range,
   --    more than Integer_32'Last points, a native index outside Points, or
   --    a failure reported by OpenCV.
   function Convexity_Defects
     (Points : Contour; Hull : Point_Index_Array) return Convexity_Defect_Array
   with
     Post =>
       Convexity_Defects'Result'Length <= Hull'Length
       and then (for all Defect of Convexity_Defects'Result =>
                   Defect.Start_Index in Points'Range
                   and then Defect.End_Index in Points'Range
                   and then Defect.Farthest_Index in Points'Range);

geometry.name: Convexity_Defects
geometry.native_signature: function Convexity_Defects (Points : Contour) return Convexity_Defect_Array
geometry.source_signature:
--  Convexity defects of Points relative to its own convex hull. Points
   --  of at most three points yield an empty result. Otherwise this is
   --  Convexity_Defects (Points, Convex_Hull_Indices (Points)), except that
   --  a hull whose indices are not monotonic, which indicates that Points is
   --  self-intersecting, raises OpenCV_Error with that diagnosis. Points is
   --  unchanged.
   --  @param Points A simple contour, with any bounds; may be empty.
   --  @return The defects, ordered by OpenCV, with every index in
   --    Points'Range and at most Points'Length defects (the postcondition):
   --    zero-based, or the null range 1 .. 0 when there are none.
   --  @exception OpenCV_Error A non-monotonic computed hull, spans beyond the
   --    fixed-point depth range, or any failure of Convex_Hull_Indices or of
   --    the native defect computation.
   function Convexity_Defects (Points : Contour) return Convexity_Defect_Array
   with
     Post =>
       Convexity_Defects'Result'Length <= Points'Length
       and then (for all Defect of Convexity_Defects'Result =>
                   Defect.Start_Index in Points'Range
                   and then Defect.End_Index in Points'Range
                   and then Defect.Farthest_Index in Points'Range);

geometry.name: Minimum_Area_Rectangle
geometry.native_signature:
function Minimum_Area_Rectangle
  (Points : Contour) return OpenCV.Rotated_Rect
geometry.source_signature:
--  Returns OpenCV's native minimum-area rotated rectangle. Center, Size,
   --  and Angle_Degrees are binary32 native results; Angle_Degrees is in
   --  degrees. OpenCV 4.13 introduced the convention also used by 5.x:
   --  angles in [-90, 0), with changed width/height assignment; 4.12 and
   --  earlier use the older representation. For ordinary nondegenerate
   --  inputs this changes the representation, not the minimum-area region.
   --  Width need not identify the same physical side across releases. Use
   --  Box_Points for geometric vertices, without assuming a starting vertex.
   --  Empty and degenerate contours preserve the native representation; no
   --  cross-version numerical equivalence is promised for degenerate cases.
   --  Points is unchanged. Inputs that would overflow native integer
   --  convex-hull arithmetic raise OpenCV_Error.
   --  @param Points The point set, with any bounds; may be empty.
   --  @return The native minimum-area rotated rectangle, every field finite
   --    and Size nonnegative.
   --  @exception OpenCV_Error Too many points or coordinates that would
   --    overflow native hull arithmetic, a non-finite or negative native
   --    field, or a failure reported by OpenCV.
   function Minimum_Area_Rectangle
     (Points : Contour) return OpenCV.Rotated_Rect;

geometry.name: Minimum_Area_Rectangle
geometry.native_signature:
function Minimum_Area_Rectangle
  (Points : Float32_Point_Array) return OpenCV.Rotated_Rect
geometry.source_signature:
--  Minimum_Area_Rectangle of a Float32 point set, with the native version
   --  convention described above and without integer rounding. OpenCV uses
   --  binary32 rotating calipers over the hull that the Float32 Convex_Hull
   --  describes, with the same handling of signed zeros and the same
   --  coordinate span limit. OpenCV allocates three binary32 values per
   --  hull vertex in signed 32-bit arithmetic, and every Float32 point can
   --  be a hull vertex, so more than Integer_32'Last / 3 points raise
   --  OpenCV_Error. OpenCV compares candidate areas in binary32, starting
   --  from FLT_MAX: when every candidate rectangle's area exceeds
   --  Float32_Value'Last (sides of about 1.8E+19 and more), it computes a
   --  non-finite rectangle, which raises OpenCV_Error, as do other
   --  non-finite or negative native fields. Points is unchanged.
   --  @param Points The point set, with any bounds; every coordinate finite.
   --    May be empty.
   --  @return The native minimum-area rotated rectangle, every field finite
   --    and Size nonnegative.
   --  @exception OpenCV_Error A NaN or infinite coordinate, more than
   --    Integer_32'Last / 3 points, an X or Y span above Float32_Value'Last,
   --    a non-finite or negative native field, or a failure reported by
   --    OpenCV.
   function Minimum_Area_Rectangle
     (Points : Float32_Point_Array) return OpenCV.Rotated_Rect;

geometry.name: Fit_Ellipse
geometry.native_signature: function Fit_Ellipse (Points : Contour) return OpenCV.Rotated_Rect
geometry.source_signature:
--  Least-squares ellipse fitted to Points by cv::fitEllipse. This is a
   --  fitted ellipse, not a minimum enclosing ellipse. The result is the
   --  rotated rectangle in which that ellipse is inscribed. Center, Size,
   --  and Angle_Degrees are native binary32 values; Angle_Degrees is in
   --  degrees. Size.Width and Size.Height are full axis lengths, not
   --  radii. Native width, height, and angle fields are preserved without
   --  normalization, axis swapping, or a preferred orientation. Negative
   --  centers are preserved. Points is unchanged. Fewer than five points
   --  raise OpenCV.OpenCV_Error. Five or more points need not be convex,
   --  uniquely ordered, or enclose nonzero area. Repeated, collinear, and
   --  other degenerate sets may still produce a finite native result,
   --  including a zero-sized rectangle. Native failures and non-finite or
   --  negative size components raise OpenCV.OpenCV_Error. OpenCV fits
   --  exactly five points with fitEllipseDirect, and more with its classic
   --  method, which perturbs the points and retries when its system is
   --  singular, as for points exactly on one conic. OpenCV 4.12 and later,
   --  including 5.x, draw that perturbation from cv::theRNG, so such
   --  results need not repeat; earlier releases perturb deterministically.
   --  @param Points At least five points, with any bounds.
   --  @return The native rotated rectangle of the fitted ellipse.
   --  @exception OpenCV_Error Fewer than five or more than
   --    Integer_32'Last / 13 points (the native classic fit sizes a buffer as
   --    `13 * n` doubles in signed 32-bit arithmetic), a non-finite or
   --    negative native field, or a failure reported by OpenCV.
   function Fit_Ellipse (Points : Contour) return OpenCV.Rotated_Rect;

geometry.name: Fit_Ellipse_AMS
geometry.native_signature: function Fit_Ellipse_AMS (Points : Contour) return OpenCV.Rotated_Rect
geometry.source_signature:
--  Ellipse fitted to Points by cv::fitEllipseAMS, the Approximate Mean
   --  Square method of Taubin. The result has Fit_Ellipse's representation:
   --  the rotated rectangle in which the ellipse is inscribed, with native
   --  binary32 center, full-axis Size, and Angle_Degrees in degrees, preserved
   --  without normalization. When AMS yields a parabola or hyperbola rather
   --  than an ellipse, OpenCV returns Fit_Ellipse_Direct's result instead.
   --  When its system is numerically singular, as can happen for points
   --  lying exactly on one conic, such as any five points, OpenCV falls back
   --  to its classic least-squares fitEllipseNoDirect. OpenCV 4.12 and later,
   --  including 5.x, first retry such a system with random perturbations
   --  from cv::theRNG, so results for such sets need not repeat, and on those
   --  releases every call advances that generator. Fewer than five points
   --  raise OpenCV_Error. Because every native path can reach
   --  fitEllipseNoDirect, which sizes a buffer as 13 * n doubles in signed
   --  32-bit arithmetic, more than Integer_32'Last / 13 points raise
   --  OpenCV_Error. Repeated, collinear, and other degenerate sets may still
   --  produce a finite native result, including a zero-sized rectangle.
   --  Native failures and non-finite or negative size components raise
   --  OpenCV_Error. Points is unchanged.
   --  @param Points At least five points, with any bounds.
   --  @return The native rotated rectangle of the fitted ellipse.
   --  @exception OpenCV_Error Fewer than five or more than
   --    Integer_32'Last / 13 points, a non-finite or negative native field,
   --    or a failure reported by OpenCV.
   function Fit_Ellipse_AMS (Points : Contour) return OpenCV.Rotated_Rect;

geometry.name: Fit_Ellipse_Direct
geometry.native_signature: function Fit_Ellipse_Direct (Points : Contour) return OpenCV.Rotated_Rect
geometry.source_signature:
--  Ellipse fitted to Points by cv::fitEllipseDirect, the Direct least
   --  squares method of Fitzgibbon, Pilu, and Fisher, which constrains the
   --  fit to an ellipse. The result has Fit_Ellipse's representation. When
   --  the system is numerically singular, or in OpenCV 4.14 and later
   --  (including 5.x) its solution is not meaningfully elliptical, OpenCV
   --  retries once with perturbed points and then falls back to its classic
   --  least-squares fitEllipseNoDirect. The perturbation is deterministic
   --  before OpenCV 4.12 and drawn from cv::theRNG in 4.12 and later,
   --  including 5.x, where every call also advances that generator. Fewer
   --  than five, or more than Integer_32'Last / 13, points raise
   --  OpenCV_Error, as for Fit_Ellipse_AMS. Degenerate sets may still produce
   --  a finite native result, including a zero-sized rectangle. Native
   --  failures and non-finite or negative size components raise OpenCV_Error.
   --  Points is unchanged.
   --  @param Points At least five points, with any bounds.
   --  @return The native rotated rectangle of the fitted ellipse.
   --  @exception OpenCV_Error Fewer than five or more than
   --    Integer_32'Last / 13 points, a non-finite or negative native field,
   --    or a failure reported by OpenCV.
   function Fit_Ellipse_Direct (Points : Contour) return OpenCV.Rotated_Rect;

geometry.name: Fit_Ellipse
geometry.native_signature:
function Fit_Ellipse
  (Points : Float32_Point_Array) return OpenCV.Rotated_Rect
geometry.source_signature:
--  Fit_Ellipse, Fit_Ellipse_AMS, and Fit_Ellipse_Direct of a Float32
   --  point set: the same native algorithms, dispatch, fallbacks, random
   --  perturbation, point counts, and result representation as the integer
   --  overloads, applied to the binary32 coordinates without rounding.
   --  OpenCV's classic and AMS fits, which all three can reach, sum the
   --  coordinates in binary32 to find their mean. An overflowing sum would
   --  hand NaN to OpenCV's solver, which without LAPACK then takes time
   --  quadratic in the number of points, so the absolute X coordinates and
   --  the absolute Y coordinates must each sum to at most `2.0**103` (about
   --  1.0E+31); larger sets raise OpenCV_Error. Native failures and
   --  non-finite or negative size components raise OpenCV_Error. Points is
   --  unchanged.
   --  @param Points At least five points, with any bounds; every coordinate
   --    finite, within the coordinate-sum bound.
   --  @return The native rotated rectangle of the fitted ellipse.
   --  @exception OpenCV_Error Fewer than five or more than
   --    Integer_32'Last / 13 points, a NaN or infinite coordinate, a
   --    coordinate sum beyond the bound, a non-finite or negative native
   --    field, or a failure reported by OpenCV.
   function Fit_Ellipse
     (Points : Float32_Point_Array) return OpenCV.Rotated_Rect;

geometry.name: Fit_Ellipse_AMS
geometry.native_signature:
function Fit_Ellipse_AMS
  (Points : Float32_Point_Array) return OpenCV.Rotated_Rect
geometry.source_signature:
--  Fit_Ellipse_AMS of a Float32 point set, with the integer overload's
   --  algorithm and fallbacks and the Float32 Fit_Ellipse rules for
   --  coordinates, counts and results. Points is unchanged.
   --  @param Points At least five points, with any bounds; every coordinate
   --    finite, within the coordinate-sum bound.
   --  @return The native rotated rectangle of the fitted ellipse.
   --  @exception OpenCV_Error Fewer than five or more than
   --    Integer_32'Last / 13 points, a NaN or infinite coordinate, a
   --    coordinate sum beyond the bound, a non-finite or negative native
   --    field, or a failure reported by OpenCV.
   function Fit_Ellipse_AMS
     (Points : Float32_Point_Array) return OpenCV.Rotated_Rect;

geometry.name: Fit_Ellipse_Direct
geometry.native_signature:
function Fit_Ellipse_Direct
  (Points : Float32_Point_Array) return OpenCV.Rotated_Rect
geometry.source_signature:
--  Fit_Ellipse_Direct of a Float32 point set, with the integer
   --  overload's algorithm and fallbacks and the Float32 Fit_Ellipse rules
   --  for coordinates, counts and results. Points is unchanged.
   --  @param Points At least five points, with any bounds; every coordinate
   --    finite, within the coordinate-sum bound.
   --  @return The native rotated rectangle of the fitted ellipse.
   --  @exception OpenCV_Error Fewer than five or more than

   function Fit_Ellipse_Direct
